chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who is killed in the way of Allah is buried in his clothes, and he is not washed unless the Muslims find him while he still has some breath left, and then he dies afterwards; in that case, he is washed, enshrouded, and embalmed. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) enshrouded Hamza in his clothes and did not wash him, but he prayed over him.'

key_terms.يُقْتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: killed in the way of Allah (martyr)

ai.seo_question: What are the funeral rites for a martyr who dies in battle according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between a martyr who dies instantly on the battlefield, who is buried in their garments without ritual washing (ghusl), and one who survives briefly before passing, requiring full funeral rites. It grounds this legal nuance in the Prophetic precedent of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, whose body was shrouded in his clothes without washing, a practice highly revered in Shia jurisprudence as a sign of honor.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The one who has been killed in the Way of Allahazwj would be buried in his clothes, and he would not be washed except if the Muslims had come across him and he still had some breath (left in him). Then if he were to die afterwards, so he would be washed, and enshrouded, and embalmed. Rasool-Allahsaww enshrouded Hamzaas in hisas clothes, and did not wash himas, but hesaww prayed Salaat upon himas’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub ibn Sinan from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘

Those who are killed in the way of Allah are buried with their clothes without Ghusl (bath) unless Muslims find him alive and then he dies afterward, in which case Ghusl (bath), shroud and hunut are done for him. The Messenger of Allah buried Hamzah with his clothes without Ghusl (bath) but he (the Messenger of Allah) performed Salah (prayer) for him.’”
